# Friction

Public app: https://friction.alx21.chatgpt.site/
Source and usage: https://github.com/agammann/friction-webmcp#readme

Friction records visual and page-side WebMCP journeys for one fixed, simulated RelayConf registration. No real booking or payment occurs. The baseline intentionally omits a confirmation requirement and full completion price. A visible approval workflow activates a fixed repair and clears the traces for retesting.

Ten tools: get_test_scenario, start_agent_run, inspect_task_state, configure_registration, review_registration, complete_simulated_task, get_human_interaction_trace, compare_human_agent_runs, submit_parity_finding, propose_interface_patch.

Start with get_test_scenario({}). Configure ticket=general_admission and seat=quiet_zone. Repaired completion requires the current reviewToken returned by review_registration plus confirmed=true. There is no remote MCP endpoint or approval tool. Proposals are visible text notes; they do not execute code.

Reports distinguish actual recorded events from labeled synthetic examples. The comparison checks records, disclosures, review, confirmation, and action counts. Action balance is a heuristic, not a usability certification. Export local JSON to preserve runs before replacing them. State uses optional browser storage and is not independently verified audit evidence.
